thread:
ella: Quick follow-up from the loader RFC — I'm prototyping a small 'bundle index' to make warmups and sparse tensor loads cheaper. idea: one tiny metadata file per bundle with compact offsets + a bloom-ish hotlist.

sam: Can you sketch the index format?

ella: super simple for now, lines: <tensor_hash> <shard_id> <file_offset> <length> <hot_score>
```
# example
ab12ff 3 1048576 65536 0.92
cd34aa 0 0 131072 0.11
```
advantages: single stat+read to learn where to fetch, reduces mmap churn, lets us prefetch only top-k hot tensors.

nguyen: Sounds promising. Two quick tradeoffs: (1) maintaining index consistency when we rewrite shards (atomic swap?), (2) extra roundtrip for bundles with tiny tensors where a full manifest might be cheaper.

ella: agreed. For atomicity I was thinking: write new shard+new index, then rename both under same txn (os rename order) and bump bundle-version meta. clients follow version pointer.

priya: What about safetensors compatibility? We need to avoid duplicating parsed metadata. Could embed index as an extra section in safetensors footer instead of a separate file.

ella: I considered footer embed but wanted ability to ship index updates without touching large weight files in some workflows. separate file is simpler for patch upgrades.

tor: Also need to quantify: how much seeks/reads saved vs extra metadata fetch. Suggest bench: 100 small tensors (avg 8KB) spread across 16 shards. Measure first-token latency, total bytes read, open file count.

sam: +1. Also test with cold vs warm kernel page cache and with mmap vs read. maybe a 'prefetch-first-n' mode on startup.

nguyen: Another angle: use a tiny in-bundle bloom filter to quickly reject misses before seeking index. That reduces IO for truly missing names in reranking scenarios.

ella: good call. I sketched hotlist as small float per tensor in index for LRU prefetch policy. We could also keep a rolling access counter on the serving side and periodically rewrite the index.

priya: Need to be careful with rewrite frequency — rewriting index often may cause churn for clients. Maybe keep a delta file for hotlist updates so main index is append-once.

ida-bot: created issue #4092: "bundle-index prototype + benchmarks" and assigned to ella, sam.

ella: thanks ida-bot. Plan: I'll prototype separate index file + prefetch worker, add bench harness per tor's matrix. If we hit >25% reduction in cold-start bytes read for typical small-tensor models, we iterate to embed vs separate file.

sam: Ping me when you have the harness. I can add kernel-page-cache toggles and a fake cloud store to simulate remote latency.

nguyen: One more thought — routing: index can expose shard affinity hints for smart routing (send request to node that already has shard hot). That could reduce network fetches in Dedicated clusters.

ella: yes! that's in the long term plan: index -> {shard_id, host_hint}. For now we'll prototype host_hint empty.

priya: For rollouts, we should add validation: index checksum + bundle-version in our model manifest. Reject mismatched pairs.

tor: volunteer to run the 16-shard bench and collect metrics.

ella: awesome — will push PR with docs + bench steps. TL;DR: bundle-index = small metadata file to reduce seeks & enable hot prefetch; prototype + benchmarks next week.

sam: :thumbsup:

priya: :eyes:

ida-bot: linked issue #4092 -> PR #5124 when opened."
